mappings.justification: PRIMARY name/tool fields identify the called function. MCP and dynamic bare names require their server/namespace qualifier for the parser canonical tool name; ordinary function/custom/output names pass through. Action.type is CONTEXT, not a competing primary name.

Explicit call_id fields pair lifecycle requests and outputs. Completed native/extension item IDs can instead identify nested operations without a matching top-level function request. They remain useful operation joins, but the entire primary set is not unconditionally the same outer call/result identifier.

Function/custom inputs are complete requests, and ordered command argv can be rendered as command text. interaction_input is stdin, and spawn_agent.arguments.items is only one component of a structured spawn request; a source leaf command[] is not itself the whole command.

Bash.timeout and Monitor.timeout_ms are configured limits in milliseconds. MonitorOutput.timeoutMs records that configured deadline/limit, with 0 explicitly meaning persistent. No seconds-to-ms transformation is required for these PRIMARY sources.

McpToolCall.server and invocation.server identify the actual target, and list_mcp_resources.server is a discovery filter. metadata.mcp_attribution.sources[].server_name is cumulative historical source provenance, explicitly not the current call server.

Agent tool results carry status async_launched (143) or completed (6-7): two of the four activity kinds (started, completed). Messaging, interruption and resumption are not given as a status; SendMessage results carry only the addressed agent (pin.id/name/ref, 89 results, never an activity kind) and resumedAgentId (54).

Function/dynamic namespace is the literal namespace. MCP connectorId identifies the connector while appName is its display name. All describe affiliation, but identifier, namespace, and display-name components are not interchangeable units. actionName is CONTEXT and does not invalidate the namespace primary by itself.
